chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “There is no valid oath in anger, nor in severing ties of kinship, nor under compulsion, nor under coercion.”
He said: I said, “May Allah keep you well, then what is the difference between coercion and compulsion?”
He said: “Compulsion is from the ruler, and coercion is from the wife, the father, and the mother, and that is of no consequence.”

key_terms.إِكْرَاهٍ: coercion or pressure, here from family members
key_terms.الزَّوْجَةِ: the wife, mentioned as a source of coercive pressure
key_terms.بِشَيْءٍ: of any consequence or legal effect
key_terms.غَضَبٍ: anger; a state in which an oath is not considered valid
key_terms.قَطِيعَةِ رَحِمٍ: severing kinship ties; a context in which an oath has no validity
key_terms.يَمِينٍ: an oath; a sworn commitment whose validity is being discussed

ai.seo_question: When is an oath invalid in Islamic law according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that an oath is not valid when made in anger, in the context of severing kinship ties, or under compulsion or coercion. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes compulsion by authority from pressure exerted by close family members, and rules that such oaths carry no binding effect.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4312 - Abdullah ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said that
Abu Abdillah (as) said: "There is no valid oath taken in anger, nor in severing ties of kinship, nor under coercion, nor under compulsion."
I asked: "May Allah (swt) keep you well, what is the difference between coercion and compulsion?"
Imam (as) replied: "Compulsion is from a ruler, while coercion can come from a wife, a father, or a mother, and such an oath is of no consequence."
